pages.text: The high river flooded the grassy bank. The goat was tethered in grass on the hill. Every evening, Raju brought it home.
Mina wanted to bring it alone, too. "I'll go today."
Mina climbed the hill and took the rope just as Raju did.
Mina pulled hard. The goat braced on all four feet.
Mina pulled with both hands. Heave-ho! The goat did not budge.
Mina sat in the grass. Their palms were red.
Raju came up and led the goat away. Mina followed down empty-handed.
In the yard, Mom said, "A goat follows grass, not the rope."
The next day, Mina picked a handful of grass and offered it at the goat's nose.
Mina walked ahead with the grass. The goat followed closely. Mina brought it home alone.
